chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Walīd ibn Abān, who said:

I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: May I perform salat (prayer) in al-fanak and al-sinjāb? He said: Yes. Then I said: May one perform salat (prayer) in foxes' skins when they have been duly slaughtered? He said: Do not perform salat (prayer) in them.

key_terms.الثَّعَالِبِ: foxes; their skins are ruled impermissible here for salat (prayer)
key_terms.السِّنْجَابِ: squirrel; its fur is mentioned here as permissible for salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْفَنَكِ: a type of fur-bearing animal whose skin is mentioned here as permissible for salat (prayer)
key_terms.ذَكِيَّةً: ritually slaughtered in a valid manner

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in fox skin or other animal furs according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from al-Riḍā عليه السلام concerning performing salat (prayer) in garments made from certain animal furs. It permits salat (prayer) in al-fanak and al-sinjāb, while forbidding salat (prayer) in fox skins even if they are ritually slaughtered.
